paper.title: AgentEvolver: Towards Efficient Self-Evolving Agent System
paper.central_claim: AgentEvolver, an RL-based self-evolving agent training system with three mechanisms (self-questioning: LLM-synthesised tasks; self-navigating: experience pool, experience-mixed rollouts and experience stripping/selective boosting; self-attributing: LLM step-wise credit assignment) improves Qwen2.5-7B/14B on AppWorld and BFCL-v3 with higher exploration efficiency and sample utilisation than vanilla GRPO.

provenance.notes: Opus aggregate seat via the configured claude-kimi type fable; no route probing. actual_model/session_id/receipt_ref are null because the subagent runtime exposes no verifiable provider receipt to this worker.

sections_read: Opus: complete pinned text read end-to-end (abstract, all sections, tables, appendices) before opening seat records; targeted re-reads for every disputed field

evidence.quote:
Autonomous agents powered by large language models (LLMs) have the potential to significantly enhance human productivity by reasoning, using tools, and executing complex tasks in diverse environments. However, current approaches to developing such agents remain costly and inefficient, as they typically require manually constructed task datasets and reinforcement learning (RL) pipelines with extensive random exploration. These limitations lead to prohibitively high data-construction costs, low exploration efficiency, and poor sample utilization. To address these challenges, we present
AgentEvolver
, a self-evolving agent system that leverages the semantic understanding and reasoning capabilities of LLMs to drive autonomous agent learning.
AgentEvolver
introduces three synergistic mechanisms: (i)
self-questioning
, which enables curiosity-driven task generation in novel environments, reducing dependence on handcrafted datasets; (ii)
self-navigating
, which improves exploration efficiency through experience reuse and hybrid policy guidance; and (iii)
self-attributing
, which enhances sample efficiency by assigning differentiated rewards to trajectory states and actions based on their contribution.
By integrating these mechanisms into a unified framework,
AgentEvolver
enables scalable, cost-effective, and continual improvement of agent capabilities. Preliminary experiments indicate that
AgentEvolver
achieves more efficient exploration, better sample utilization, and faster adaptation compared to traditional RL-based baselines.

evidence.quote:
In the context of agent self-evolution, an
experience
encapsulates distilled insights derived from past trajectories, encompassing both successful and unsuccessful cases. In our setting, we formalize an
experience
as a unit of structured knowledge articulated in natural language, designed to guide agents toward appropriate decisions through In-Context Learning (ICL). Each
experience
comprises two components:
When to use
and
Content
. The
When to use
component specifies the conditions under which the experience is applicable and serves as a retrieval trigger, with queries semantically matching to its vectorized embedding. The
Content
component provides detailed instructions, precautions, or recommended strategies for effective action within that context. Representing experiences entirely in natural language preserves interpretability while supporting scalable, embedding-based retrieval.
evidence.support_explanation: 持久非权重对象是带适用触发条件与内容的自然语言经验。

evidence.quote:
(1)
trajectory preprocessing
, where collected trajectories are validated and classified into success and failure groups according to their scores;
(2)
experience extraction
, where task memories are distilled from successful, failed, or comparative trajectory pairs, capturing essential behavioral insights;
(3)
experience validation
, which employs an LLM-based evaluator to assess the quality and reliability of each extracted experience; and
(4)
vector store updating
, where validated task experiences are indexed and integrated into the long-term experience storage for subsequent retrieval and reasoning.
evidence.support_explanation: 按轨迹结果分组、提炼、LLM 质量校验、写入长期向量库；这是质量门，不是边际收益门。

evidence.quote:
To seamlessly integrate the benefits of retrieved experiences into RL training, we propose an
experience incorporation
mechanism that operates during the optimization stage. This mechanism comprises two complementary components:
experience stripping
and
selective boosting
. The former prevents spurious dependence on explicit textual cues, while the latter amplifies the influence of pertinent constructive experiences. In combination, these procedures ensure that experience effectively guides policy learning while mitigating the peril of over-reliance on external prompts.

Experience Stripping

While experience-guided rollouts leverage extracted experience by injecting it into the input prompt, retaining these tokens during optimization risks undesirable overfitting, as the model may memorize external content rather than assimilating its underlying reasoning signals. To address this, we adopt an
experience stripping
strategy: prior to policy gradient computation, retrieved experience tokens are removed from the training samples. This ensures that optimization is driven exclusively by the generated trajectory, thus attributing reward signals to the model’s intrinsic reasoning processes rather than auxiliary contextual cues. Consequently, the rollout phase continues to benefit from experience, whereas the training phase fosters genuine policy improvement.
evidence.support_explanation: 经验先条件化 rollout，再剥离经验 token 计算策略梯度，明确耦合接口及分布错配风险。

evidence.quote:
We begin by examining whether incorporating retrieved experiences during inference can improve the quality of generated trajectories without additional training.
Specifically, we measure trajectory quality by the rewards obtained, which naturally reflect task success.
As illustrated in Figure
13(a)
, results on both AppWorld and BFCL consistently demonstrate that past experiences provide strong navigation signals: they stabilize rollouts and raise the performance ceiling, yielding average gains of
↑
\uparrow
5.4% avg@4
and
↑
\uparrow
6.7% best@4
.
Collectively, these results underscore the
value of leveraging experience as an external compass: even without training, contextualized guidance allows the model to explore more effectively and produce superior outcomes.

G.reason: out_of_scope (rubric A3 bullet 1; Opus sides with son55 on the scope conflict). The evaluated object is the GRPO-trained policy: all main and ablation results (Tables 1–3, 5, the 'w/ RL' rows of Table 4) are trained checkpoints (opus:O01, O02), and evaluation is explicitly run without experience (opus:O03). The non-weight experience pool exists, but in this paper it is a rollout aid: retrieved experience is injected only into training rollouts and stripped before the gradient (opus:O04), the pool is a cold-start pool built from the initial policy on synthetic tasks with construction delegated to the external ReMe implementation (opus:O05, O06), and the authors present explicit (in-context) use as the inferior path that RL 'internalizes' (opus:O07). The only evaluation of the pool as an artifact read at inference is one dev-set row (Table 4 'w/o RL + exp.', opus:O08) plus Figure 13(a) — a side check on a frozen model, not the claim, and on the dev split. Self-questioning tasks and the LLM judge are training data/rewards for weights (r08a ASL, r07b 2511.03773, r05b SEAgent precedent); the context templates (Table 7) are static within-episode options. This differs from r08a EvolveR / r06b LatentEvolve, whose evaluated systems read the retained store at test with a store-off arm. Flip condition: the evaluated agent reads the pool at test, or the pool is evaluated as a claimed artifact on held-out tasks with a store-off arm. Not scored; null is not a zero-quality rating.

The non-weight experience pool exists, but in this paper it is a rollout aid: retrieved experience is injected only into training rollouts and stripped before the gradient (opus:O04), the pool is a cold-start pool built from the initial policy on synthetic tasks with construction delegated to the external ReMe implementation (opus:O05, O06), and the authors present explicit (in-context) use as the inferior path that RL 'internalizes' (opus:O07). The only evaluation of the pool as an artifact read at inference is one dev-set row (Table 4 'w/o RL + exp.', opus:O08) plus Figure 13(a) — a side check on a frozen model, not the claim, and on the dev split. Self-questioning tasks and the LLM judge are training data/rewards for weights (r08a ASL, r07b 2511.03773, r05b SEAgent precedent); the context templates (Table 7) are static within-episode options. This differs from r08a EvolveR / r06b LatentEvolve, whose evaluated systems read the retained store at test with a store-off arm. Flip condition: the evaluated agent reads the pool at test, or the pool is evaluated as a claimed artifact on held-out tasks with a store-off arm. Not scored; null is not a zero-quality rating.
